A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the chloride ion, which was present in the reaction media in both cases, had an impact on the final products.

The main takeaway from our work is that
the hydrogen-bonding of the COOH terminus is a key factor in the formation of a {Mo2O2Cl2}2+ unit, which is a common structural motif in many molybdena-containing enzymes.
the presence of the chloride counterion in the reaction mixture is crucial to the formation of the chloride salt of the {Mo2O2Cl4}3− complex.
, in contrast to the common carboxylic acid dimers, the hydrogen-bonded linkers between the COOH functions and the anionic species are not limited to the halogen anions.
